characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material; flow stress (and peak stress) increases with ε̇ and decreases with T. Experimental phenomena were reproducible.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); cylindrical Φ 8 mm × 12 mm specimen; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on the end faces
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire rheological (flow stress) curves and study the hot deformation / dynamic recrystallization behaviour of the steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Degree of DRX ranked zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation); DRX grain size increases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T; at low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) DRX is insufficient with large original grains retained.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, then prepared, ground, polished and etched; three deformation zones (1 difficult, 2 small, 3 large deformation) observed with 100 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure evolution and measure the DRX average grain size in the deformation zones
characterization_methods.technique: optical / laser confocal microscopy of etched cross-sections

analytical_models.equation_role: relate strain rate, peak stress and temperature; basis for the DRX activation energy
analytical_models.model_note: Qp is reported as the average value within the experimental range; the fitted lines in Fig. 4 were not well parallel, indicating a significant effect of deformation conditions on the activation energy.

analytical_models.equation_role: compute DRX activation energy from the average fitted slopes
analytical_models.model_note: k1 and k2 are the average slopes of the ln(ε̇) vs ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T linear fits, respectively (Fig. 4).

analytical_models.equation_role: characterise the combined effect of T and ε̇ on flow stress
analytical_models.model_note: Table 1 lists lnZ for all T/ε̇ combinations; the value for this sample (900 °C, 1 s^-1) is 68.69. lnZ increases with increasing ε̇ and decreasing T.

analytical_models.equation_role: relate the critical, peak and steady-state stresses/strains of the flow curve to lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Multiple-linear-regression fits; fitting quality R(critical)=0.947, R(peak)=0.957, R(steady)=0.956 and R(strains) 0.911–0.922 (Fig. 6). These models are established for the steel across the full T/ε̇ matrix; the paper does not tabulate the individual values for 900 °C/1 s^-1.

analytical_models.equation_role: determine the critical strain εc for DRX initiation from the flow curve
analytical_models.model_note: εc = εp·(√(1−C) − (1−C))/C (Eq. 9); the derived εc/εp ≈ 0.452 is consistent with literature using the θ–σ inflection point.

analytical_models.equation_role: predict DRX average grain size as a function of strain rate and temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Obtained by Levenberg-Marquardt regression of the experimental data; R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%. Initial grain size and strain treated as fixed constants.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: α = β/n1 = 0.00599; gas constant R = 8.314 J·(mol·K)^-1. DEFORM-3D simulation: billet set as a rigid plastic body, die indenter as a rigid body, semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; frictional condition at the billet/die interface = shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air = 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C).
computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis with the Zener-Hollomon parameter; Cingara-McQueen analysis for critical strain; multiple linear regression; Levenberg-Marquardt optimization for the grain-size model
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D (finite-element software used for the DRX average grain-size prediction model)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For the DRX average grain-size prediction model the correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and the mean relative error (MRE) for all samples = 4.53%; the absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size is mostly within 3 µm.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cylindrical sample (Φ 8 mm × 12 mm) heated at 10 °C/s up to the 1200 °C homogenisation temperature.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 900 °C at 5 °C/s; this sample's set T is 900 °C (its sample_label/aliases).
Held at the set T (900 °C) for 15 s before compression so the inside/outside temperature difference was eliminated.
Strain rate = 1 s^-1 (this sample's ε̇). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricant were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: heterogeneous/inhomogeneous — mixture of fine DRX grains and large remnant original grains; homogeneity poor at this low-T/high-ε̇ condition

phases_present.morphology: small equiaxed DRX grains together with large, elongated remnant original grains

microstructure_list.region: core of the compressed sample = large deformation zone (zone 3)

structures.overall_structure: Insufficiently dynamically recrystallized (partial DRX) microstructure. At the low deformation temperature (900–950 °C) and high strain rate (1–10 s^-1) regime, the DRX grains are small but DRX is not sufficient and large-sized original grains remain, giving poor microstructural homogeneity. The measured grain size is taken from the core of the compressed sample (large deformation zone).

unmapped_findings: lnZ for this sample (T = 900 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1) is 68.69 (Table 1); lnZ increases with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature, so this condition lies at the high-Z (harder-to-recrystallize) end of the experimental matrix.

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T; peak stress can be lowered by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0084).
The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ·mol^-1 (b0012, b0085).

Peak stress for the specific 900 °C/1 s^-1 condition is not tabulated in the text; from the 3D peak-stress map for ε̇ = 1–10 s^-1 (Fig. 3d, colour bar 94.00–486.0 MPa) the 900 °C region is at the high end of the scale (b0024, figure_003). At 900 °C the peak stress at 0.01 s^-1 was 305.4 MPa (b0024), and at 1150 °C it fell to 53.8 MPa at 0.01 s^-1 (82% reduction) and by 73% at 10 s^-1.

Optimal hot-working conditions for a fine and uniform grain structure are 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086). This sample (900 °C/1 s^-1) lies outside these windows.
At low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but DRX is insufficient and large original grains remain, giving poor microstructure homogeneity (b0063).
According to the DRX state diagram (Fig. 7), as lnZ increases the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs both increase, i.e. starting and completing DRX becomes more difficult (b0058).

The experimental results (including reproducibility, checked by repeating isothermal compression on the same steel batch under identical conditions) were stated to be reproducible (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0065).
The initial (pre-deformation) microstructure consists of large polygonal grains with fine parallel striations (segregation/dendritic banding) and no numeric grain size is reported (figure_001).
